content: For patients whose A1C level is 1.5% or more above their individualized target, it is frequently necessary to implement combination therapy to achieve optimal glycemic control. This therapeutic approach typically involves the use of pharmacological agents with high efficacy. Examples of such agents include GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists (GIP/GLP-1 RAs), and sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors. These medications, when used in combination, not only help in achieving better glycemic regulation but also provide additional benefits by addressing cardiovascular health, which is a critical consideration in diabetes management.
